attribution: Calculated by Environment Dashboard from Climate TRACE (2026), Climate TRACE Emissions Inventory v5.10.0, https://climatetrace.org [2026-10-08], doi:10.5281/zenodo.22919723, licensed CC BY 4.0. Includes EDGAR CH4, N2O and F-gases v8.0 (© European Union, European Commission Joint Research Centre, CC BY 4.0) and FAOSTAT emissions totals (FAO, CC BY 4.0) as reproduced by Climate TRACE. Changes: converted to million tonnes; world values summed from every country; methane and nitrous oxide of subsectors taken from EDGAR converted to CO₂-equivalent with IPCC AR6 100-year global warming potentials, their carbon dioxide left out; other manufacturing left out. Subsectors grouped into activities; the five added.
description: Climate TRACE's emissions of all greenhouse gases from the five activities Bill Gates uses in How to Avoid a Climate Disaster, added together, for the world and each country, 2016–2025: the total that each share in ghg.climate-trace.by-activity-share is a percentage of. Like Gates's total (Rhodium Group's), it counts emissions from human activity before what land takes up and without wildfires. Carbon dioxide from the subsectors Climate TRACE takes from EDGAR, and other manufacturing, are not included, so it is somewhat smaller than all emissions.
notice: Solid waste disposal includes landfill reports from the US EPA (FLIGHT and the Landfill Methane Outreach Program), the European Pollutant Release and Transfer Register (European Environment Agency) and Canada's Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program, and contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence - Canada. Carbon dioxide that Climate TRACE takes from IEA-EDGAR CO2 is not included.

processing.description: Read the country-level CSV of each of 68 subsectors of Climate TRACE Emissions Inventory V5.10.0 (Zenodo record 22919723), by HTTP range requests from each subsector's zip: <gas>/DATA/<subsector>_country_emissions_v5_10_0.csv. Checked the columns, that every row names its own sector, subsector and gas, is in tonnes, covers one calendar year, and that each of the 252 codes has one row in every year 2015–2026.

Used the 100-year CO₂-equivalent file (co2e_100yr, IPCC AR6 global warming potentials) for aluminum, bauxite-mining, cement, chemicals, coal-mining, copper-mining, crop-residues, domestic-aviation, domestic-shipping, domestic-wastewater-treatment-and-discharge, electricity-generation, enteric-fermentation-cattle-operation, enteric-fermentation-cattle-pasture, enteric-fermentation-other, food-beverage-tobacco, forest-land-clearing, forest-land-degradation, forest-land-fires, glass, heat-plants, industrial-wastewater-treatment-and-discharge, international-aviation, international-shipping, iron-and-steel, iron-mining, lime, manure-applied-to-soils, manure-left-on-pasture-cattle, manure-management-cattle-operation, manure-management-other, net-forest-land, net-shrubgrass, net-soil-organic-carbon, net-wetland, non-broadcasting-vessels, non-residential-onsite-fuel-usage, oil-and-gas-production, oil-and-gas-refining, oil-and-gas-transport, other-agricultural-soil-emissions, other-chemicals, other-metals, other-mining-quarrying, petrochemical-steam-cracking, pulp-and-paper, removals, residential-onsite-fuel-usage, rice-cultivation, road-transportation, rock-quarrying, sand-quarrying, shrubgrass-fires, synthetic-fertilizer-application, textiles-leather-apparel, water-reservoirs, wetland-fires, wood-and-wood-products, and for fluorinated-gases (EDGAR F-gases, CO₂-equivalent only).

For the subsectors Climate TRACE takes from EDGAR (biological-treatment-of-solid-waste-and-biogenic, cropland-fires, incineration-and-open-burning-of-waste, other-energy-use, other-fossil-fuel-operations, other-onsite-fuel-usage, other-solid-fuels, other-transport, railways, solid-waste-disposal) read only the methane and nitrous oxide files (EDGAR CH4 and N2O, CC BY 4.0) and converted them to CO₂-equivalent with the IPCC AR6 100-year global warming potentials Climate TRACE applies: nitrous oxide 273; methane 27.0 for biological-treatment-of-solid-waste-and-biogenic, cropland-fires, incineration-and-open-burning-of-waste, solid-waste-disposal; methane 29.8 for other-energy-use, other-fossil-fuel-operations, other-onsite-fuel-usage, other-solid-fuels, other-transport, railways. Their carbon dioxide is IEA-EDGAR CO2, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, and is not included anywhere: these subsectors are methane and nitrous oxide only.

Left out other-manufacturing entirely: Its carbon dioxide is IEA-EDGAR CO2 (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0) and its other gases mix EDGAR with plant reports from the European, US and Israeli pollutant registers, so they cannot be separated by producer.

The country totals of food-beverage-tobacco, glass, heat-plants, lime, non-residential-onsite-fuel-usage, other-chemicals, other-metals, other-mining-quarrying, residential-onsite-fuel-usage, road-transportation, textiles-leather-apparel, wood-and-wood-products are built by Climate TRACE from EDGAR, CEDS or IEA World Energy Balances inputs (IEA energy statistics); Climate TRACE publishes them under CC BY 4.0 and they are used under that licence.

Climate TRACE publishes no world rows. The world value of a subsector and year is the sum of all 252 country rows, including UNK (vessels whose country is not known), which is published under no country; it is missing if any row is missing. Kosovo (XKX) and Northern Cyprus (ZNC) are Climate TRACE's own codes.
Left out 2026: its rows cover January to June only (V5.10.0 was released on 27 August 2026 with Climate TRACE's 60-day lag).

Treated as missing, not zero: net-soil-organic-carbon 2015, removals 2025, net-forest-land 2025, net-shrubgrass 2025, net-wetland 2025, where V5.10.0 writes 0 for every country because those land fluxes were not yet estimated. 1,260 country-years are missing in all.

Published as Climate TRACE gives them, and flagged: subsector years in which every country's value equals the year before, where Climate TRACE carries its EDGAR, FAOSTAT or other input forward: heat-plants 2024, 2025; other-fossil-fuel-operations 2025; non-broadcasting-vessels 2016; enteric-fermentation-other 2024, 2025; manure-management-other 2024, 2025; biological-treatment-of-solid-waste-and-biogenic 2025; incineration-and-open-burning-of-waste 2025.

Grouped the subsectors into Gates's five activities and three bands that are not one of the five, following Rhodium Group's grouping behind the book's shares (fuel supply under making things, waste with growing things, fluorinated gases with keeping warm and cool, electricity where generated, forest fires left out). Making things: aluminum (Aluminium smelting); cement (Cement); chemicals (Ammonia, methanol and soda ash plants); food-beverage-tobacco (Food and drink factories); glass (Glass); iron-and-steel (Steel); lime (Lime); other-chemicals (Other chemical industry); other-metals (Metals other than iron, steel and aluminium); petrochemical-steam-cracking (Ethylene and other plastic feedstocks); pulp-and-paper (Paper); textiles-leather-apparel (Textiles and clothing); wood-and-wood-products (Sawmills and wood products); bauxite-mining (Mining the ore of aluminium); copper-mining (Mining copper ore); iron-mining (Mining iron ore for steel); other-mining-quarrying (Other mines and quarries); rock-quarrying (Quarrying stone for building); sand-quarrying (Quarrying sand for concrete and glass); coal-mining (Methane from coal mines; Rhodium counts fuel supply under industry); oil-and-gas-production (Venting, flaring, leaks and fuel use at oil and gas fields; fuel supply); oil-and-gas-refining (Refineries; Rhodium counts refining under industry); oil-and-gas-transport (Pipelines and liquefied gas; fuel supply); other-fossil-fuel-operations (EDGAR's other fuel supply); other-solid-fuels (Coke ovens, charcoal and other solid-fuel making; fuel supply). Plugging in: electricity-generation (Power plants making electricity); heat-plants (District heat plants; IPCC and Rhodium count heat with electricity); other-energy-use (EDGAR's other energy industries; Rhodium counts it with electricity). Growing things: crop-residues (Crop residues left on fields); cropland-fires (Burning crop residues in fields); enteric-fermentation-cattle-operation (Methane from cattle in feedlots); enteric-fermentation-cattle-pasture (Methane from grazing cattle); enteric-fermentation-other (Methane from other livestock); manure-applied-to-soils (Manure spread on fields); manure-left-on-pasture-cattle (Cattle dung on pasture); manure-management-cattle-operation (Cattle manure stored at feedlots); manure-management-other (Manure of other livestock); other-agricultural-soil-emissions (Farmed soils, including drained organic soils); rice-cultivation (Methane from flooded rice fields); synthetic-fertilizer-application (Nitrous oxide from fertiliser); biological-treatment-of-solid-waste-and-biogenic (Composting and digestion; Rhodium groups waste with agriculture); domestic-wastewater-treatment-and-discharge (Sewage; Rhodium groups waste with agriculture); incineration-and-open-burning-of-waste (Burning waste; Rhodium groups waste with agriculture); industrial-wastewater-treatment-and-discharge (Factory wastewater; Rhodium groups waste with agriculture); solid-waste-disposal (Landfill methane; Rhodium groups landfills with agriculture); forest-land-clearing (Clearing forest, mostly for farming; gross carbon released); forest-land-degradation (Logging and thinning forests); net-soil-organic-carbon (Carbon lost or gained by cropland soils (net)). Getting around: domestic-aviation (Flights within a country); domestic-shipping (Ships within a country); international-aviation (Flights between countries, counted in the country of departure); international-shipping (Ships between countries); non-broadcasting-vessels (Ships without transponders, seen by radar satellites); other-transport (EDGAR's other transport, such as pipelines and off-road vehicles); railways (Trains); road-transportation (Cars, trucks and buses). Keeping warm and cool: non-residential-onsite-fuel-usage (Fuel burned in offices, shops and public buildings); other-onsite-fuel-usage (EDGAR's other fuel use in buildings and farms; Rhodium counts it with buildings); residential-onsite-fuel-usage (Fuel burned in homes for heat, hot water and cooking); fluorinated-gases (Refrigerants and other fluorinated gases; Rhodium counts refrigerants under buildings). Not one of the five: wildfires: forest-land-fires (Forest fires; Rhodium leaves them out); shrubgrass-fires (Grassland and savanna fires; as forest fires); wetland-fires (Wetland and peat fires; as forest fires). Not one of the five: land taking up carbon: removals (Carbon taken up by standing forests; a sink, not an activity); net-forest-land (Net carbon change of forest that stays forest); net-shrubgrass (Net carbon change of shrub and grassland that stays so); net-wetland (Net carbon change of wetland that stays wetland). Not one of the five: reservoirs: water-reservoirs (Methane from dam reservoirs for power, water and irrigation alike).

A group's value is the sum of its subsectors; it is missing in any place and year in which any of its subsectors is missing, never a partial sum. Land taking up carbon is kept as its own band and never subtracted from the five.

Added the five activities (making things, plugging in, growing things, getting around, keeping warm and cool) in the same place and year; missing where any of the five is missing. Wildfires, land taking up carbon and reservoirs are not included. Converted tonnes to million tonnes by dividing by 1,000,000 (exact decimal arithmetic).

scope.basis: Climate TRACE V5.10.0 country-level estimates (modelled, mostly from satellite and other remote sensing and facility data, revised every month), 100-year global warming potentials from the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report. Some subsectors' country totals are built by Climate TRACE from EDGAR, CEDS or IEA World Energy Balances inputs (road transport, residential and non-residential buildings, heat plants, glass, lime, food, textiles, other chemicals, other metals, wood, other mining) and are used under Climate TRACE's CC BY 4.0. For the subsectors Climate TRACE takes from EDGAR (other energy use, railways, other transport, other onsite fuel use, other solid fuels, other fossil fuel operations, landfills, composting, waste burning, cropland fires) only methane and nitrous oxide are included: their carbon dioxide is IEA-EDGAR CO2, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Other manufacturing is not included. 2026 is a partial year and is not shown. International aviation and shipping are included. Land use is shown in parts: clearing and degrading forest (gross carbon released) and the net carbon change of cropland soils; wildfires; and carbon taken up by standing forests with the net change of forest, shrub and grassland, and wetland that stays as it is (below zero where land takes up carbon). In V5.10.0 the 2025 values of that uptake are not yet estimated and are missing.
scope.geography: The world and 251 countries and territories (international aviation and shipping assigned to countries)
